neighbours.label: the word 'slap' in any form or sense ('Sl|ap Shot', ' slap', ' slapped', ' slap|stick')
fire: The boss will slap a heavy fine on the driver.
The man slapped the table and shouted for more beer.
The children call that rash 'slap cheek' at school.
Old comedy films are full of slapstick and pie fights.
The hockey player took a hard Slap Shot from the line.
Do not slap your brother on the back of his head.
My mother slapped my hand when I reached for the cake.
That new law is just a slap on the wrist for banks.
quiet: The boss will put a heavy load on the driver.
The man tapped the table and asked for more beer.
The children call that game 'tag' at school.
Old comedy films are full of music and bright dancing.
The hockey player took a long rest on the line.
Do not poke your brother on the back of his head.
My mother held my hand when I reached for the cake.
That new law is just a burden on the budget for banks.

notes: Card: ' slap' x14, 'lag' x5, ' slapped' x4, 'ap' x3, 'ack' x3, 'apped'. Probe: 'ap' of Slap and slap 0.901-1.001; ' slap' 0.814-0.841; ' slapped' 0.595; put, kissed and flag or back or shack at most 0.008. 'lag' and 'ack' are not covered.
